project.audience: motor insurance policyholders and claims staff

input:
Claims modernisation — workshop summary (v2)

Context: Today motor claims are filed by phone and take 21 days on average to settle. Goal: settle simple claims in under 48 hours.
Actors: policyholder, claims handler, assessor, garage partner, fraud team.

1. Policyholders file a claim in the mobile app: policy lookup, incident date/location, description, photos/video of damage, third-party details.
2. Claims under ₹50,000 with no injury and no third party are 'simple' and go to auto-assessment: an AI damage estimate from photos, then a handler approves the payout.
3. Everything else goes to a handler queue, prioritised by severity; handlers can request an assessor visit.
4. Garage partners receive repair jobs, submit quotes and invoices through a partner portal.
5. Fraud team gets a flag on claims matching risk rules (e.g. policy started < 30 days ago, repeated claims); flagged claims cannot be auto-approved.
6. Policyholders see claim status and get notified at each stage (WhatsApp preferred).
7. Payouts via bank transfer to the account on file.

NFRs: available 24/7; documents encrypted at rest; full audit trail of every decision; must integrate with the existing policy admin system (SOAP API, nightly batch only).

Open: Legal hasn't confirmed whether an AI estimate can be used without a human looking at the photos.

requirements: file a claim in the mobile app
upload photos and video of damage
garage partner portal for quotes and invoices
claim status notifications at each stage
questionsAbout: legal approval for AI damage estimates
keeping policy data current with a nightly batch
what happens when the AI estimate and the garage quote differ
conflicts: policy lookup at claim time vs policy admin system updated only by nightly batch
mustNotInvent: a specific uptime percentage stated as explicit
